title: Ten other ways to draw a Python for-loop
brief: Represent `for other in others` as dataflow while keeping the collection, current element, loop-carried pose, and final pose temporally honest. Zach’s dotted header-spine proposal is the fixed reference; these are ten structural alternatives, not color variants.
defaultWhy: Paired Gates leads at 95.2/100: it gives collection unpacking, carried values, recurrence, completion, break, and nesting distinct homes while leaving the body as ordinary dataflow.
decisionHinge: The result hinges on how much grammar should live in the frame. Move 10 points from semantic completeness to SystemSketch fit and 5 from hard-loop scalability to visual calm: Paired Gates and Header Lanes tie at 92.2. If the common case is one accumulator and shallow nesting, prefer Header Lanes; if break, multiple carries, or nesting are normal, keep Paired Gates.
invariants: Zach’s latest dotted header-spine sketch remains the external reference and is not counted among the ten alternatives.
Solid cable means usable in the current invocation; amber dotted cable means available only after an iteration boundary.
Every direction uses the same `others` + seed `pose` + `merge()` fixture.
The internal body remains an ordinary SystemSketch dataflow graph.
boundary: These are editable visual-grammar prototypes and an authored `.systemsketch` stress board. They do not add a loop shape, execution semantics, parser rule, or Python round-trip implementation to the product.

requirements.name: Semantic completeness
requirements.why: The notation must expose the collection, current element, initial state, recurrence, and final value without relying on remembered code.
requirements.passCondition: A reader can point to each role and explain when it is available.

anchors.1: One or more loop roles are absent or conflated.
anchors.3: All roles are inferable, but at least one depends on convention or prose.
anchors.5: Every role has a distinct visible home and timing.

requirements.name: Turn clarity at a glance
requirements.why: The core ambiguity is whether a value is usable now or only after an iteration boundary.
requirements.passCondition: Solid same-turn flow and cross-turn recurrence cannot be mistaken for one another.

anchors.1: The diagram plausibly implies an impossible same-turn read.
anchors.3: Timing is marked but needs careful tracing.
anchors.5: The temporal boundary is immediate and local.

requirements.name: Hard-loop scalability
requirements.why: The grammar should survive destructuring, multiple carried values, conditional updates, early exit, and nesting.
requirements.passCondition: The five stress programs extend the same rule instead of inventing a new notation.

anchors.3: Two hard cases fit with crowding or special cases.
anchors.5: All five fit through repetition of the same primitives.

requirements.name: Visual calm
requirements.why: Loop marks should not overwhelm the body graph or turn one carried value into a bundle of crossing arrows.
requirements.passCondition: The loop reads in one scan with few long or overlapping cables.

anchors.1: The control notation dominates or crosses the body.
anchors.3: Readable at normal scale with some route management.
anchors.5: Compact, local, and visually subordinate to the body.

requirements.name: SystemSketch fit
requirements.why: A strong direction should reuse Blocks, ports, Pills, regions, and delayed/dotted edges rather than introduce a second visual language.
requirements.passCondition: The idea can be built as a narrow extension of the current canvas vocabulary.

anchors.1: Requires a foreign editor or a parallel graph model.
anchors.5: Composes existing SystemSketch objects and edge semantics.

hardGates.name: Collection ≠ current element
hardGates.why: The whole iterable and the item available this iteration must never share one undifferentiated cable.

hardGates.name: Seed / next / final are distinct
hardGates.why: A carried value has three temporal roles and the representation must not collapse them.

hardGates.name: No impossible same-turn read
hardGates.why: A returned value may feed the next iteration or the final exit, not the current invocation that produced it.

hardGates.name: Body remains dataflow
hardGates.why: The loop notation should schedule an ordinary internal dataflow graph rather than replace it with prose.

variants.name: Paired Gates
variants.thesis: Put iteration on a paired Input/Yield boundary: one gate exposes current items and state; the other receives next state and owns completion.
variants.bestWhen: Structured loops with carried values, completion, break, or nesting.
variants.losesWhen: A tiny single-use loop where two extra boundary nodes feel heavier than the body.

variants.name: Header Lanes
variants.thesis: Turn the loop header into two typed lanes—each and carry—then drop short local wires into the body.
variants.bestWhen: The loop body is visually primary and the header can carry several named values.
variants.losesWhen: Nested loops or many carries make the header dense and text-dependent.

variants.losesWhen: Break, continue, side effects, or nesting no longer fit the fold abstraction cleanly.

variants.losesWhen: A synchronous Python loop could be mistaken for asynchronous scheduling.
